title: Random forest MRI radiomics predicts clinically significant prostate cancer
summary: Random forest radiomics models on MRI from 1616 patients at four centers predicted clinically significant prostate cancer with AUCs of 0.874 (internal test) and 0.876 and 0.893 (external tests). Adjusting PI-RADS with the model improved AUC and specificity at a slight cost to sensitivity, and the Rad-score correlated with ISUP grade (r > 0.600). The study is retrospective, and the authors state prospective validation is still needed.
